Compute a common regular time grid across a cohort of samples

Source: R/preprocess.R
compute_common_time_grid.Rd

Chooses a regular RT grid suitable for resampling every sample onto shared row indices. Row i in the resampled Z always corresponds to physical time target_time[i] regardless of which sample the row came from — the prerequisite for pixel-consistent cross-sample encoder input.

Usage

compute_common_time_grid(samples, step = 1, t_max = NULL)

Arguments

samples

List of samples (each with a $time numeric vector).

step

Grid step in seconds. See details.

t_max

Maximum RT for the grid (seconds). See details.

Value

Numeric vector of RT positions in seconds, evenly spaced by step, starting at 0, ending at >= max sample time.

Details

Grid choice:

  • step: distance in seconds between consecutive rows. Default 1.0 — physically meaningful (row index = seconds), adequate for typical GC-DMS peak FWHM (~2-5 s), and roughly matches current native RT dimensions (~1500 rows). Common alternatives: 0.5 (double resolution), median(diff(time)) from the cohort, or "median" / "mean" which computes the median / mean per-row time delta across all samples.

  • t_max: maximum RT (seconds) on the returned grid. Default NULL uses max(unlist(lapply(samples, [[, "time"))) — the longest sample's endpoint, so no sample is truncated. Rounded up to the nearest integer multiple of step.
